claim: Bcl-2 family proteins reorganize mitochondrial membranes during apoptosis to form pores and rearrange cristae.
source: Bcl-2 family proteins reorganize mitochondrial membranes during apoptosis, to form pores and rearrange cristae.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established background knowledge about Bcl-2 family proteins.

claim: Loss of full-length Bid results in apoptosis-independent, irregular cristae with decreased respiration.
source: Loss of full-length Bid results in apoptosis-independent, irregular cristae with decreased respiration.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Bid-/- mice display stress-induced myocardial dysfunction and damage.
source: Bid-/- mice display stress-induced myocardial dysfunction and damage.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by echocardiography and histology data in the results.

claim: Decreased genetically determined BID expression associates with myocardial infarction (MI) susceptibility.
source: A gene-based approach applied to a biobank, validated in two independent GWAS studies, reveals that decreased genetically determined BID expression associates with myocardial infarction (MI) susceptibility.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by PrediXcan analysis in the results section.

claim: Patients in the bottom 5% of BID expression distribution exhibit >4 fold increased MI risk.
source: Patients in the bottom 5% of the expression distribution exhibit >4 fold increased MI risk.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by analysis of BioVU data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Carrier status with nonsynonymous variation in Bid's membrane binding domain, BidM148T, associates with MI predisposition.
source: Carrier status with nonsynonymous variation in Bid's membrane binding domain, BidM148T, associates with MI predisposition.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by exome-chip analysis in BioVU shown in Figure 8.

claim: Bid associates with Mcl-1Matrix.
source: Furthermore, Bid but not BidM148T associates with Mcl-1Matrix, previously implicated in cristae stability
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 9.

claim: Decreased MCL-1 expression associates with MI.
source: decreased MCL-1 expression associates with MI
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 9.

claim: Mitochondrial membranes can reorganize with changes in metabolic conditions.
source: In addition to cell death, mitochondrial membranes can reorganize with changes in metabolic conditions (Hackenbrock, 1966) (Mannella, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Regulation of the inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM) into highly organized loops known as cristae is necessary for a multitude of metabolic processes.
source: Regulation of the inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM) into highly organized loops known as cristae is necessary for a multitude of metabolic processes (Cogliati et al., 2016)(Rampelt et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Cristae harbor respiratory chain complexes embedded within and peripheral to the membrane.
source: Cristae harbor respiratory chain complexes embedded within and peripheral to the membrane and this tight organization is critical for efficient electron transfer (Lapuente-Brun et al., 2013) and cytochrome c sequestration (Korsmeyer et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Tight organization of cristae is critical for efficient electron transfer and cytochrome c sequestration.
source: Cristae harbor respiratory chain complexes embedded within and peripheral to the membrane and this tight organization is critical for efficient electron transfer (Lapuente-Brun et al., 2013) and cytochrome c sequestration (Korsmeyer et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Inefficient oxidative phosphorylation due to disruption of the respiratory chain can lead to mitochondrial disease.
source: Inefficient oxidative phosphorylation due to disruption of the respiratory chain can lead to mitochondrial disease, which range widely in organ systems and severity (Moslehi et al., 2012; Picard et al., 2016; Wallace, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: During apoptosis, Bid is cleaved by caspase-8 to form cBid.
source: During apoptosis, the BH3-only protein Bid, is cleaved by caspase-8 (cBid) to facilitate both mitochondrial cristae reorganization (Cogliati et al., 2013; Frezza et al., 2006; Scorrano et al., 2002) and outer membrane permeability (Gross et al., 1999; Li et al., 1998; Luo et al., 1998; Walensky et al., 2006; Wang et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: cBid facilitates both mitochondrial cristae reorganization and outer membrane permeability.
source: During apoptosis, the BH3-only protein Bid, is cleaved by caspase-8 (cBid) to facilitate both mitochondrial cristae reorganization (Cogliati et al., 2013; Frezza et al., 2006; Scorrano et al., 2002) and outer membrane permeability (Gross et al., 1999; Li et al., 1998; Luo et al., 1998; Walensky et al., 2006; Wang et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: cBid associates with Bax and Bak through its BH3-domain at the outer mitochondrial membrane.
source: cBid associates with the multidomain Bcl-2 proteins Bax and Bak through its BH3-domain at the outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM), triggering mitochondrial outer membrane pores (MOMP) (Gross et al., 1999; Li et al., 1998; Luo et al., 1998; Walensky et al., 2006; Wang et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Bid's role in regulating cristae structure has been limited to in vitro studies focusing on isolated mitochondria and cBid.
source: Bid's role in regulating cristae structure has been limited to in vitro studies focusing on isolated mitochondria and cBid.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of prior research.

claim: cBid's interaction with the mitochondrial membrane is stabilized in part through an interaction with MTCH2 and cBid's membrane binding domain (MBD).
source: cBid's interaction with the mitochondrial membrane is stabilized in part through an interaction with MTCH2 as well as cBid's membrane binding domain (MBD), consisting of alpha-helices 4,5, and 6 (Tae-Hyoung Kim, Yongge Zhao, Wen-Xing Ding, Kim et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Alpha-helix-6 partially embeds within the membrane.
source: Alpha-helix-6 partially embeds within the membrane (Oh et al., 2005), and has been shown to be necessary for apoptotic cristae reorganization (Cogliati et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Alpha-helix-6 has been shown to be necessary for apoptotic cristae reorganization.
source: Alpha-helix-6 partially embeds within the membrane (Oh et al., 2005), and has been shown to be necessary for apoptotic cristae reorganization (Cogliati et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Bid is involved in the regulation of other essential cellular processes such as DNA damage and metabolism, acting as rheostat for cell health.
source: In addition to its apoptotic function, Bid is also known to be involved in the regulation of other essential cellular processes such as DNA damage and metabolism, acting as rheostat for cell health (Reviewed in Giménez-Cassina and Danial, 2015; Hardwick et al., 2012; Zinkel et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Full-length Bid can localize to the mitochondria.
source: Interestingly, full-length Bid can also localize to the mitochondria (Maryanovich et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Bid-/- MPCs display decreased growth rates due to decreased viability, not altered proliferation.
source: Consistent with a pro-survival function, Bid-/- myeloid progenitor cells (MPCs) display decreased growth rates not due to altered proliferation, but instead as a result of decreased viability (p<0.05) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–c).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mitochondria in Bid-/- MPCs are highly abnormal compared to Bid +/+ MPCs.
source: Compared to Bid +/+ MPCs, mitochondria in Bid-/- MPCs were highly abnormal.
evidence: This is supported by TEM images shown in Figure 2.

claim: Bid-/- MPCs have a significant decrease in the number of cristae compared to Bid +/+ MPCs.
source: Quantitation of the average number of cristae per mitochondrion revealed a significant decrease in the number of cristae in Bid-/- MPCs compared to Bid +/+ MPCs (p<0.0001) (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of TEM images shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Bid-/- MPCs stably expressing FHA-BidBH3 can rescue cristae structure.
source: This function is independent of Bid's apoptotic role, as Bid-/- MPCs stably expressing Flag-HA-tagged full-length Bid mutated in either in its BH3-domain (FHA-BidBH3) or caspase-8 cleavage site D59 (FHA-BidD59A) could rescue cristae structure (p<0.0001) (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of TEM images shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Bid-/- MPCs stably expressing FHA-BidD59A can rescue cristae structure.
source: This function is independent of Bid's apoptotic role, as Bid-/- MPCs stably expressing Flag-HA-tagged full-length Bid mutated in either in its BH3-domain (FHA-BidBH3) or caspase-8 cleavage site D59 (FHA-BidD59A) could rescue cristae structure (p<0.0001) (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of TEM images shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Bid's cristae regulation function is independent of Bid's apoptotic role.
source: This function is independent of Bid's apoptotic role, as Bid-/- MPCs stably expressing Flag-HA-tagged full-length Bid mutated in either in its BH3-domain (FHA-BidBH3) or caspase-8 cleavage site D59 (FHA-BidD59A) could rescue cristae structure (p<0.0001) (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is inferred from the ability of BH3 and D59A mutants to rescue cristae structure.

claim: Bid-/- cells have a slight decrease in mitochondrial density per cell compared to Bid+/+ cells.
source: Furthermore, quantitation of the area density of mitochondria per cell revealed a slight decrease in density in the Bid-/- cells compared to Bid+/+ cells (p<0.05), while FHA-BidD59A expressing cells had increased mitochondrial density compared to all other cell lines (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claim: FHA-BidD59A expressing cells have increased mitochondrial density compared to all other cell lines.
source: Furthermore, quantitation of the area density of mitochondria per cell revealed a slight decrease in density in the Bid-/- cells compared to Bid+/+ cells (p<0.05), while FHA-BidD59A expressing cells had increased mitochondrial density compared to all other cell lines (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Overexpression of full-length WT Bid but not FHA-BidBH3 or FHA-BidD59A results in the production of endogenous cBid in the absence of a death stimulus.
source: Indeed, overexpression of full-length WT Bid (Bid-/- + FHA Bid) but not FHA-BidBH3 or FHA-BidD59A results in the production of endogenous cBid in the absence of a death stimulus (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: In a myeloid cell line, Bid's apoptotic domains must be mutated to fully restore cristae.
source: Thus, in a myeloid cell line, we observe that Bid's apoptotic domains must be mutated to fully restore cristae.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that WT Bid produces cBid and fails to rescue cristae, while BH3 and D59A mutants succeed.

claim: Loss of Bid does not lead to compensatory upregulation of Bim, Bad, or Puma in MPCs or LV cardiac tissue.
source: We evaluated Bid-/- cellular extracts as well as lysate from left ventricular (LV) cardiac tissue which are highly enriched in mitochondria, and find no compensatory upregulation of Bim, Bad, or Puma to account for the observed loss of cristae structure in Bid-/- cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2b and c).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2b and c.

claim: Full-length Bid is found in a heavy membrane, mitochondrial-enriched fraction absent of cytosolic contamination.
source: We find full-length Bid in a heavy membrane, mitochondrial-enriched fraction absent of cytosolic contamination (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is supported by subcellular fractionation data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Full-length Bid is observed in mitochondria isolated from liver tissue, both in a crude mitochondrial fraction and in a Percoll purified fraction.
source: We also observe full-length Bid in mitochondria isolated from liver tissue, both in a crude mitochondrial fraction as well as in a Percoll purified fraction (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: A pool of Bid remains uncleaved with Proteinase K treatment under conditions in which Bak is cleaved.
source: We observe that a pool of Bid remains uncleaved with PK, under conditions in which we observe cleaved Bak (Figure 3c), a protein associated with the OMM.
evidence: This is supported by Proteinase K treatment data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Bid is enriched in the mitoplast-containing fraction compared to the OMM.
source: We find an enrichment of Bid in the mitoplast-containing fraction compared to the OMM (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is supported by mitochondrial subfractionation data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Full-length Bid can localize to the mitochondria during non-apoptotic conditions and is found both at the OMM as well as in the mitoplast.
source: Taken together, the above results suggest that full-length Bid can localize to the mitochondria during non-apoptotic conditions and is found both at the OMM as well as in the mitoplast.
evidence: This is inferred from the fractionation and Proteinase K experiments.

claim: Mitochondria cristae defects in humans can result in severe abnormalities in multiple organ systems, especially the heart.
source: Mitochondria cristae defects in humans can result in severe abnormalities in multiple organ systems, especially the heart (Brown et al., 2017; Meyers et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Left ventricular tissue isolated from Bid-/- mice reveals striking irregularities both in gross mitochondrial organization between myofibrils as well as loss of normal lamellar cristae structure.
source: TEM of left ventricular tissue isolated from Bid-/- mice revealed striking irregularities both in gross mitochondrial organization between myofibrils as well as loss of normal lamellar cristae structure (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is supported by TEM images shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Without treatment, Bid-/- tissue has overall decreased mitochondrial electron density corresponding to significantly increased cristae width.
source: Specifically, without treatment, Bid-/- tissue had overall decreased mitochondrial electron density corresponding to significantly increased cristae width (p<0.0001) (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of TEM images shown in Figure 4b.

claim: 18 hours after 0.5 mg/kg Epinephrine treatment, both Bid+/+ and Bid-/- tissues are damaged, but the Bid-/- cristae are significantly more deformed.
source: We assessed both Bid+/+ and Bid-/- mitochondria 18 hr after a dose of 0.5 mg/kg Epi and find that while both Bid+/+ and Bid-/- tissues are damaged, the Bid-/- cristae are significantly more deformed (p<0.0001) (Figure 4a and b).
evidence: This is supported by TEM images and quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4a and b.

claim: Damaged cristae in Bid-/- mice after Epinephrine treatment are structurally similar to mitochondria observed after induction of an acute myocardial infarction.
source: Interestingly, these damaged cristae are structurally similar to mitochondria observed after induction of an acute myocardial infarction (MI) (Bryant et al., 1958).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature describing MI-induced mitochondrial damage.

claim: Bid-/- mice have a severe cardiac cristae defect that results in increased susceptibility to acute stress-induced damage.
source: Thus, Bid-/- mice have a severe cardiac cristae defect that results in increased susceptibility to acute stress-induced damage.
evidence: This is inferred from the TEM data showing increased cristae damage in Bid-/- mice after Epinephrine treatment.

claim: Cardiac function does not differ between Bid+/+ and Bid-/- mice at baseline.
source: Cardiac function does not differ at baseline.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by echocardiography data in Figure 4.

claim: 18 hours after acute Epinephrine treatment, Bid-/- mice show a significant increase in left internal ventricular diameter during diastole (LVIDd) compared to Bid+/+ mice.
source: However, we find a significant increase in left internal ventricular diameter during diastole (LVIDd) (p<0.01) as well as during systole (LVIDs) (p<0.05) 18 hr after Epi (Figure 4c and d).
evidence: This is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: 18 hours after acute Epinephrine treatment, Bid-/- mice show a significant increase in left internal ventricular diameter during systole (LVIDs) compared to Bid+/+ mice.
source: However, we find a significant increase in left internal ventricular diameter during diastole (LVIDd) (p<0.01) as well as during systole (LVIDs) (p<0.05) 18 hr after Epi (Figure 4c and d).
evidence: This is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: 18 hours after acute Epinephrine treatment, Bid-/- mice show a significant decrease in Ejection Fraction (EF) compared to Bid+/+ mice.
source: This corresponds to a significant decrease in Ejection Fraction (EF) for Bid-/- mice (p<0.01) (Figure 4e)
evidence: This is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: 18 hours after acute Epinephrine treatment, Bid-/- mice show an increase in both end diastolic and end systolic volume compared to Bid+/+ mice.
source: Furthermore, we also observe an increase in both end diastolic (p<0.01) and end systolic volume (p<0.05) (Figure 4f and g) with stress.
evidence: This is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 4f and g.

claim: Decreased LV cardiac function observed in Bid-/- mice is phenotypically similar to observations made by echo in patients during the acute phase of MI.
source: Decreased LV cardiac function observed in Bid-/- mice is phenotypically similar to observations made by echo in patients during the acute phase of MI (LV wall dilation and decreased ejection fraction) (White et al., 1987; Di Bella et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature describing MI phenotypes in humans.

claim: At 5 days post-Epinephrine, both Bid+/+ and Bid-/- mice have restored cardiac function.
source: Interestingly, at 5 days post-Epi, both the Bid+/+ and Bid-/- mice had restored cardiac function and we find no difference in heart weights at sacrifice (Figure 4c–g and Figure 4—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 4c-g.

claim: Doxorubicin treatment results in a significant decrease in fractional shortening (FS) and ejection fraction (EF) in Bid-/- mice.
source: Dox also resulted in a significant decrease in FS and EF (p<0.01) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c and d) in Bid-/- mice.
evidence: This is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1c and d.

claim: Using two different models (Epinephrine and Doxorubicin), Bid plays a role in maintaining LV function under stress.
source: Thus, using two different models, Epinephrine, which directly results in increased oxygen demand, as well as the mitochondrial toxic drug Doxorubicin, we find that Bid plays a role in maintaining LV function under stress.
evidence: This is inferred from the echocardiography data showing decreased cardiac function in Bid-/- mice under both Epinephrine and Doxorubicin stress.

claim: Myocardial fibrosis due to cardiomyocyte remodeling after damage is a prominent sequelae of MI and directly contributes to loss of cardiac function.
source: Myocardial fibrosis due to cardiomyocyte remodeling after damage is a prominent sequelae of MI, and directly contributes to loss of cardiac function (Talman and Ruskoaho, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Bid-/- tissue has significantly increased fibrosis both at 18 hours and 5 days post Epinephrine treatment.
source: We find that Bid-/- tissue has significantly increased fibrosis both at the 18 hr and the recovery time point, 5 days post treatment (p<0.05) (Figure 5b and c).
evidence: This is supported by Masson's trichrome staining and quantitation shown in Figure 5b and c.

claim: WT mice display no increase in fibrosis at 18 hours post-Epinephrine; fibrosis develops in WT hearts at 5 days post-Epinephrine.
source: Interestingly, WT mice display no increase in fibrosis at 18 hr post-Epi; fibrosis developed in WT hearts at 5 days post-Epi.
evidence: This is supported by Masson's trichrome staining and quantitation shown in Figure 5.

claim: Bid-/- mice have more fibrosis and increased susceptibility to damage after stress.
source: Thus, Bid-/- mice have more fibrosis and increased susceptibility to damage after stress.
evidence: This is inferred from the fibrosis quantitation data.

claim: Although Bid-/- mice are able to recover functionally after Epinephrine stress, the long-term damage is more severe.
source: This result recapitulates the response to cardiomyocyte damage in human MI and suggests that although the Bid-/- mice are able to recover functionally, the long-term damage is more severe.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cardiac function recovers but fibrosis persists in Bid-/- mice.

claim: MudPIT analysis identified 54 significantly different mitochondrial proteins between Bid+/+ and Bid-/- MPC samples.
source: Cross referencing our hits to the Mouse MitoCarta 2.0 (Calvo et al., 2016), we identified 54 significantly different mitochondrial proteins between the Bid+/+ and Bid-/- samples (Figure 6—figure supplement 1b and c).
evidence: This is supported by MudPIT proteomics data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Bid-/- heart mitochondria show a decrease in the activity of ATP synthase dimers.
source: We observe a decrease in the activity of ATP synthase dimers from Bid-/- heart mitochondria (p<0.05) (Figure 6a and b)
evidence: This is supported by in-gel activity assay data shown in Figure 6a and b.

claim: The decrease in ATP synthase dimer activity is consistent with the known association between dimerization of ATP synthase in cristae loop formation and stabilization of cristae structure.
source: We observe a decrease in the activity of ATP synthase dimers from Bid-/- heart mitochondria (p<0.05) (Figure 6a and b), consistent with the known association between dimerization of ATP synthase in cristae loop formation and stabilization of cristae structure (Hahn et al., 2016; Paumard et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Bid-/- heart mitochondria show a significant decrease in the activity of complex I within the supercomplexes.
source: We observed a significant decrease in the activity of complex I within the SCs and a trend for decreased activity of complex IV containing SCs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1d,e and f).
evidence: This is supported by in-gel activity assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1d, e, and f.

claim: Bid-/- MPCs display significantly decreased oxygen consumption rates (OCR) compared to Bid+/+ cells.
source: Using an Oroboros Oxygraph, we found Bid-/- MPCs displayed significantly decreased oxygen consumption rates (OCR) compared to Bid+/+ cells (p=0.008)
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: Respiration can be restored in Bid-/- MPCs by re-introduction of FHA-BidBH3.
source: Respiration could be restored in Bid-/- MPCs by re-introduction of FHA-BidBH3 and FHA-BidD59A but not FHA-Bid into Bid-/- MPCs (Bid-/- v. Bid-/- + FHA-BidBH3, p<0.0001 and Bid-/- v. FHA-BidD59A, p=0.0008) (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: Respiration can be restored in Bid-/- MPCs by re-introduction of FHA-BidD59A.
source: Respiration could be restored in Bid-/- MPCs by re-introduction of FHA-BidBH3 and FHA-BidD59A but not FHA-Bid into Bid-/- MPCs (Bid-/- v. Bid-/- + FHA-BidBH3, p<0.0001 and Bid-/- v. FHA-BidD59A, p=0.0008) (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: Baseline mitochondrial and cellular superoxide do not differ between Bid-/- and Bid +/+ MPCs.
source: We assessed baseline mitochondrial and cellular superoxide with MitoSOX and DHE, respectively, and found no difference between Bid-/- and Bid +/+ MPCs
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2a and c.

claim: Mitochondrial superoxide is increased in Bid-/- cells under conditions of nutrient withdrawal.
source: however mitochondrial superoxide was increased in Bid-/- cells under conditions of nutrient withdrawal (p<0.01) (Figure 6—figure supplement 2a,b and c).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2b.

claim: Bid's phosphorylation sites S61 and S78 have been shown to correspond with increased ROS and respiration in hematopoietic stem cells.
source: Bid's phosphorylation sites S61 and S78 (BidAA) have also been shown to correspond with increased ROS and respiration in hematopoietic stem cells (Maryanovich et al., 2012),(Maryanovich et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: FHA-BidBH3AA MPCs do not have altered membrane potential compared to BidBH3.
source: We find that compared to BidBH3, FHA-BidBH3AA MPCs do not have altered membrane potential and show only a trend for increased ROS (p=0.1956) (Figure 6—figure supplement 2d and e).
evidence: This is supported by TMRE staining data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2d.

claim: The results in MPCs are most consistent with a role for S61 and S78 phosphorylation sites in overall cell viability by preventing caspase-8 cleavage of Bid, rather than specifically in the regulation of mitochondrial membrane potential or ROS production.
source: Thus, our results in MPCs are most consistent with a role for these phosphorylation sites in overall cell viability, by preventing caspase-8 cleavage of Bid (Desagher et al., 2001), rather than specifically in the regulation of mitochondrial membrane potential or ROS production.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that BidBH3AA cells are unstable and do not show significant changes in membrane potential or ROS.

claim: Bid-/- LV fibers display significantly decreased oxygen consumption compared to Bid+/+ LV fibers in state 3 respiration.
source: Bid-/- LV fibers also displayed significantly decreased oxygen consumption compared to Bid+/+ LV fibers (p=0.0103) (Figure 6d).
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 6d.

claim: Bid-/- permeabilized cardiac fibers have decreased respiratory function and decreased ATP production in the presence of complex I substrates.
source: Bid-/- fibers had decreased respiratory function as well as decreased ATP production (p<0.05) (Figure 6e and f) compared to Bid +/+ fibers.
evidence: This is supported by simultaneous ATP and O2 consumption measurements shown in Figure 6e and f.

claim: Bid-/- permeabilized cardiac fibers have decreased respiration and decreased ATP production in the presence of rotenone and succinate.
source: Bid-/- PmFBs had decreased respiration in the presence of rotenone and succinate (p<0.001), and decreased ATP production (p<0.05) (Figure 6e and f)
evidence: This is supported by simultaneous ATP and O2 consumption measurements shown in Figure 6e and f.

claim: Despite an overall decrease in respiration and ATP production, Bid-/- permeabilized cardiac fibers have similar oxidative phosphorylation efficiency to Bid +/+ when using complex I substrates.
source: Interestingly, despite an overall decrease in respiration and ATP production, Bid-/- PmFBs have similar efficiency to Bid +/+ when using CI substrates.
evidence: This is supported by ATP/O ratio calculations shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2f.

claim: In the presence of rotenone and succinate, Bid-/- permeabilized cardiac fibers have an increased ATP/O ratio.
source: However, in the presence of rotenone and succinate, Bid-/- PmFBs have an increased ATP/O ratio (p<0.05) (Figure 6—figure supplement 2f).
evidence: This is supported by ATP/O ratio calculations shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2f.

claim: Bid-/- mitochondria may compensate by bypassing complex I in favor of respiratory complex II, which is not found in respiratory supercomplexes and therefore would be less impacted by disorganized cristae.
source: This suggests Bid-/- mitochondria may compensate by bypassing complex I in favor of respiratory complex I I, which is not found in respiratory supercomplexes (Schägger and Pfeiffer, 2001) and therefore would be less impacted by disorganized cristae.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased ATP/O ratio in the presence of rotenone and succinate, and supported by a citation.

claim: Decreased BID expression is significantly associated with MI in BioVU.
source: Consistent with our findings in mice, we observed that decreased BID expression is significantly associated with MI (Figure 7b).
evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 7b.

claim: The BID heritability estimate is significant (h2 = 0.08 with standard error [SE] of 0.026).
source: The BID heritability estimate was significant (h2 = 0.08 with standard error [SE] of 0.026), providing support for genetic regulation (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a and b).
evidence: This is supported by heritability analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Individuals with the lowest 5% of BID expression have a > 4 fold increase in the prevalence of myocardial infarction compared to the rest of the Synthetic Derivative.
source: Within this group, we find a > 4 fold increase in the prevalence of myocardial infarction compared to the rest of the Synthetic Derivative (Figure 7b).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of BioVU data shown in Figure 7b.

claim: Decreased BID expression in heart tissue significantly associates with myocardial infarction (p=7.55×10−3).
source: Decreased BID expression in heart tissue significantly associated with myocardial infarction (p=7.55×10−3) as well as coronary atherosclerosis (p=8.26×10−3), and ischemic heart disease (p=9.7×10−4) (Figure 7b).
evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 7b.

claim: Decreased BID expression in heart tissue significantly associates with coronary atherosclerosis (p=8.26×10−3).
source: Decreased BID expression in heart tissue significantly associated with myocardial infarction (p=7.55×10−3) as well as coronary atherosclerosis (p=8.26×10−3), and ischemic heart disease (p=9.7×10−4) (Figure 7b).
evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 7b.

claim: Decreased BID expression in heart tissue significantly associates with ischemic heart disease (p=9.7×10−4).
source: Decreased BID expression in heart tissue significantly associated with myocardial infarction (p=7.55×10−3) as well as coronary atherosclerosis (p=8.26×10−3), and ischemic heart disease (p=9.7×10−4) (Figure 7b).
evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 7b.

claim: There is no significant association between BID genetically determined expression and atrial fibrillation (p=0.63).
source: Notably, we find no significant association between BID genetically determined expression and atrial fibrillation in this dataset (p=0.63), consistent with the lack of significant association in BioVU.
evidence: This is supported by S-PrediXcan analysis of atrial fibrillation GWAS data.

claim: BID's effect is specific to particular cardiac pathophysiologies.
source: Thus, while we identify multiple cardiac traits associated with BID expression, BID's effect is specific to particular pathophysiologies.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that BID associates with MI but not atrial fibrillation.

claim: A significant correlation (p=0.002) exists between decreased genetically determined BID expression in the aorta and MI in a separate BioVU sample set.
source: In a separate BioVU sample set (see Materials and methods and Figure 7—figure supplement 1c and d), we observed a significant correlation (p=0.002) between decreased genetically determined BID expression in the aorta and MI.
evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis in a validation cohort shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1c and d.

claim: Decreased genetically determined expression of BID in heart is associated (p=0.02, effect size = −0.06, SE = 0.026) with MI in CARDIoGRAMplusC4D.
source: Consistent with the BioVU discovery and validation results, decreased genetically determined expression of BID in heart was associated (p=0.02, effect size = −0.06, SE = 0.026) with MI in CARDIoGRAMplusC4D.
evidence: This is supported by S-PrediXcan analysis of CARDIoGRAMplusC4D data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3a.

claim: No association with MI in CARDIoGRAMplusC4D was observed with BCL2L13 (p=0.75).
source: However, no association with MI in CARDIoGRAMplusC4D was observed with BCL2L13 (p=0.75) (Figure 7—figure supplement 3a and b), consistent with the SNPs being regulatory for BID.
evidence: This is supported by S-PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3a.

claim: A significant association was observed between carrier status for any missense variant in BID and MI (p=0.013; OR 1.7 [95% CI 1.1–2.6]).
source: In multivariable logistic regression, a significant association was observed between carrier status (i.e. presence of any missense variant) and MI (p=0.013; OR 1.7 [95% CI 1.1–2.6]).
evidence: This is supported by exome-chip analysis in BioVU shown in Figure 8b.

claim: Carrier status for MBD variants is strongly associated with MI (p=0.002; OR 8.5 [95% CI 2.1–33.6]).
source: Carrier status for MBD variants (i.e. presence of any missense variant in the MBD) was strongly associated with MI (p=0.002; OR 8.5 [95% CI 2.1–33.6]) (Figure 8b and c).
evidence: This is supported by exome-chip analysis in BioVU shown in Figure 8b and c.

claim: M148T was associated with MI risk (p=0.029, OR = 1.47) in a meta-analysis of exome-chip studies involving 42,335 patients and 78,240 controls of European ancestry.
source: Notably, M148T was also associated with MI risk (p=0.029, OR = 1.47) in the recent meta-analysis of exome-chip studies involving 42,335 patients and 78,240 controls of European ancestry, consistent with the BioVU results (Stitziel et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a meta-analysis study.

claim: The M148T mutation in BidBH3 fails to restore cristae structure in Bid-/- MPCs.
source: We evaluated mitochondrial cristae number in Bid +/+, Bid-/- + FHA-BidBH3 and Bid-/- + FHA-BidBH3M148T (double mutant) as in Figure 2, and found that the double mutant had significantly less cristae compared to FHA-BidBH3 alone (p<0.01).
evidence: This is supported by TEM and quantitation shown in Figure 8e, f, and g.

claim: The BidBH3/M148T double mutant has an increase in overall mitochondrial area density per cell, likely as a compensatory mechanism for decreased cristae function.
source: Interestingly, we found that the double mutant had an increase in overall mitochondrial area density per cell, likely as a compensatory mechanism for decreased cristae function (p<0.01) (Figure 8e–g).
evidence: This is supported by quantitation shown in Figure 8g, with speculation about the mechanism.

claim: Expression of the BidBH3/M148T double mutant is insufficient to restore respiratory levels comparable to Bid +/+ or Bid-/- + FHA-BidBH3 MPCs.
source: Expression of the BidBH3/M148T double mutant was insufficient to restore respiratory levels comparable to Bid +/+ or Bid-/- + FHA-BidBH3 MPCs (Figure 8h).
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 8h.

claim: BidBH3/E120D MPCs have equivalent respiration compared to BH3-mutated Bid.
source: Compared to BH3-mutated Bid, BidBH3/E120D MPCs had equivalent respiration.
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1d.

claim: BidBH3/R124Q MPCs have decreased respiration compared to BH3-mutated Bid, but not significantly different from WT MPCs.
source: While BidBH3/R124Q MPCs had decreased respiration (Figure 8—figure supplement 1d), it was not significantly different from WT MPCs.
evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1d.

claim: Neither BidBH3/E120D nor BidBH3/R124Q MPCs display altered sensitivity to TNF-α/Actinomycin D stimulated cell death.
source: Neither BidBH3/E120D nor BidBH3/R124Q MPCs displayed altered sensitivity to TNF-α/Actinomycin D stimulated cell death (Figure 8—figure supplement 1e and f).
evidence: This is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1e and f.

claim: Mcl-1 has a matrix isoform involved in respiratory chain maintenance and mitochondrial metabolism.
source: In particular, the anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family member Mcl-1 has been shown to have a matrix isoform involved in respiratory chain maintenance and mitochondrial metabolism (Escudero et al., 2018; Perciavalle et al., 2012; Thomas et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The BH3-domain of cBid associates with Mcl-1 to inhibit apoptosis.
source: It is known that the BH3-domain of cBid associates with Mcl-1, to inhibit apoptosis (Clohessy et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: FlagHA-tagged Bid can immunoprecipitate WT Mcl-1, Mcl-1OM, and Mcl-1Matrix.
source: Using FlagHA-tagged Bid expressed in 293 T cells, we were able to immunoprecipitate all three forms of Mcl-1 (Figure 9a).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9a.

claim: Bim does not associate with Mcl-1Matrix.
source: This is in contrast to the other BH3-only protein Bim, which did not associate with Mcl-1Matrix (Perciavalle et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: FHA-BidM148T displays decreased association with Mcl-1Matrix compared to both WT-Bid and FHA-BidD59A.
source: We find that FHA-BidM148T displays decreased association with Mcl-1Matrix compared to both WT-Bid and our rescue mutant, FHA-BidD59A.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9b.

claim: FHA-BidM148T displays increased association with WT Mcl-1 relative to either WT Bid or FHA-BidD59A.
source: Furthermore, FHA-BidM148T displays increased association with WT Mcl-1 relative to either WT Bid or FHA-BidD59A (Figure 9b).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9b.

claim: The results are consistent with a role for helix-6 in Bid's association with Mcl-1Matrix in the context of the mitochondrial cristae.
source: The above results are consistent with a role for helix-6 in Bid's association with Mcl-1Matrix, in the context of the mitochondrial cristae.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-immunoprecipitation data showing differential binding of BidM148T to Mcl-1Matrix.

claim: Loss of Mcl-1 has been shown to result in cardiomyopathy.
source: Loss of Mcl-1 has previously been shown to result in cardiomyopathy (Wang et al., 2013) and impaired autophagy leading to heart failure in mice (Thomas et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Decreased genetically determined expression of MCL-1 is significantly associated with MI (p=0.00903).
source: We find that decreased genetically determined expression of MCL-1 is significantly associated with MI (p=0.00903) (Figure 9c).
evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 9c.

claim: MTX1 has reduced genetically determined expression significantly associated with MI (p=1.93×10−5).
source: In addition to MCL-1, we find that MTX1 (Metaxin1), a mitochondrial protein transporter that associates with the MICOS complex (Guarani et al., 2015), has reduced genetically determined expression significantly associated with MI (p=1.93×10−5).
evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 9c.

claim: Patients with a history of cardiomyopathy have a significantly increased relative risk for MI compared to known risk factors.
source: Interestingly, we find that patients with a history of cardiomyopathy have a significantly increased relative risk for MI compared to the known risk factors, connecting these two phenotypes genetically (Figure 9d).
evidence: This is supported by contingency table analysis shown in Figure 9d.

claim: Bid may perform its role at the mitochondrial matrix through interaction with Mcl-1.
source: Finally, we find an association between Bid and the matrix form of Mcl-1 mediated by the helix-6 residue M148, suggesting that Bid may perform its role at the mitochondrial matrix through interaction with Mcl-1.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-immunoprecipitation data and the functional studies.
